THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 20.11.2010, passed by the tribunal, in MVC No.1060/2006, seeking enhancement of compensation.

2. Heard the arguments and perused the material placed before the Court.
3.
The factum of accident, claimant sustaining injuries in the said accident and coverage of insurance are not in dispute in this case.
4. Learned counsel for appellant/claimant submitted that in the present case the claimant has suffered fracture of 2nd, 3rd and 4th ribs.
But the tribunal NC: 2023:KHC-D:9167 awarded compensation of Rs.5,000/- only and prays for enhancement of compensation.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent insurance company submitted that so far as fracture of ribs are concerned, initially it is mentioned in the case sheet that there is no fracture on the chest but later on it was written down fracture of ribs.
Therefore the case of the claimant is unbelievable.
Hence, justified the compensation awarded by the tribunal.
6. It is proved that in Ex.P.5 wound certificate there is no mentioning of injuries caused to the chest and fracture of ribs.

In Ex.P.17 case sheet, initially it was written down upon x-ray taken on chest Sri Vasant S/O Ramachandra Shinde vs The Managing Director on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125106537/

sentences.text: there are no fracture seen but in the case sheet it is written that upon x-ray taken it is seen fracture of 2nd, 3rd and 4th ribs of right side.
Soon after the accident the claimant was admitted to the City Civil Hospital, Belagavi and the doctor who treated him is examined as PW.3.
The doctor of City Civil Hospital, Belagavi, who has treated the claimant is NC: 2023:KHC-D:9167 examined as PW.3 and he has stated that sometimes fractures may go unnoticed.

Sometimes only it can be apparent as a tenderness injury and at initial point of time fractures were unnoticed but when the pain is continuous and persisting for some considerable length of time, then there would be an occasion for taking x-ray for second time and that is what has been revealed in the present case.
Therefore upon taking x-ray for second time it is found that the claimant had suffered fracture of 2nd, 3rd and 4th ribs of right side.
7. Just because in the wound certificate if fracture of ribs is not mentioned, that cannot be said that there are no fracture of ribs.
The contention in the wound certificate are written based on the case sheet what is noted down in the case sheet.
Soon after admitted to the hospital, there may be chances of going unnoticed fractures and that may not have been mentioned in the wound certificate.
But the evidence on record show that upon x-ray taken for 2nd time, it is noticed that the claimant has suffered fracture NC: 2023:KHC-D:9167 of ribs on the right side.

Therefore,
considering this evidence of PW.3 doctor and Ex.P.17 case sheet and Ex.P.16 x-ray, it is proved that the claimant had suffered fracture of 2nd, 3rd and 4th ribs and accordingly he has to be compensated.
8. The tribunal has awarded only global compensation of Rs.5,000/-.
It requires to be modified.
Considering the nature of injuries suffered, a compensation of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head injuries, pain and suffering.

Since the claimant has taken treatment in Government hospital,
and even though the treatment is free but sometimes the patient may be constrained to purchase medicine from outside from the medical shops since all the medicines cannot be available in the Government hospital.
Therefore considering this reality aspect a compensation of Rs.5,000/- is awarded under the head medical expenses.

Further, a compensation of Rs.7,000/- is awarded for incidental expenses like food, nourishment, conveyance, attendant NC: 2023:KHC-D:9167 charges,
etc.,.
Further, a compensation of Rs.15,000/- is awarded under the head loss of amenities.

9. The claimant is a mechanic by profession and the doctor has stated that the claimant suffered 15%
of physical disability towards chest region and the claimant being a mechanic by profession,
certainly the fracture to ribs is affecting the working capacity of the claimant, which may result into affecting the earning capacity also.
Therefore, 5% is taken as functional disability affecting loss of future income/earning capacity due to disability.
The accident is of the year 2006 and in the absence of proof of income, Rs.3,750/- per month is to be taken which is recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
The claimant was aged 56 years at the time of accident.
Therefore appropriate applicable multiplier is 9.
Hence, loss of earning capacity due to disability is assessed and quantified as Rs.20,250/- (Rs.3,750 x 5% x 12 x 9).

sentences.text: Further, a compensation of Rs.7,500/- is awarded towards loss of income during laid up and treatment period for a period of two months.

11. Thus, the claimant is entitled for total compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads. Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Towards injuries, pain and 20,000  suffering.
 2. Towards medical expenses.
5,000  3. Towards loss of amenities.

15,000  4. Towards loss of income during 7,500  laid up and medical treatment  period.
 5. Towards incidental charges like 7,000  attendant charges, food,
nourishment, conveyance, etc.,.
6 . Towards loss of future earning 20,250 capacity.

Therefore, the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.74,750/- as against Rs.5,000/-
awarded by the tribunal.

The claimant is entitled for interest on the compensation at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
The NC: 2023:KHC-D:9167 * respondent No.1 N.W.K.R.T.C is directed to deposit the amount of compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this judgment.

13. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award dated 20.11.2010, passed by the MACT, Khanapur, in MVC No.1060/2006, stands modified to the aforesaid extent.
iii) The claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.74,750/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization, as against Rs.5,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
iv) The claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 109 days in filing the appeal.
Corrected, vide court order dated 06.12.2023 SD/-

vi) The * respondent No.1 N.W.K.R.T.C shall pay the compensation to the claimant within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
 vii) No order as to costs.
viii) Draw award accordingly.
